Spain’s socialist leader hopes the demonstrations will galvanize support for his party ahead of elections this month. The housing crunch has worsened during his latest term, as it has across much of Europe: Renting a one-bedroom apartment in central Madrid costs about three-quarters of the average salary , with dozens of cities surpassing the 30% threshold generally considered optimal. Owning has gotten more expensive too as interest rates rise and persistent red tape makes new-home construction almost impossible. Demonstrators hope to seize on the moment. “ A historic window of opportunity has opened ,” one said. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

articles.summary: World leaders convene in Antalya, Turkey, on Monday for the United Nations’ 31st Conference of the Parties, or COP31 , after another year of deadly climate disasters. Forest fires in Canada , Indonesia , and Brazil impacted millions of people. Heat waves contributed to more than 50,000 deaths in Europe. Floods prompted by the collapse of a melting glacier killed more than 1,500 people in Nepal and caused nearly $5 billion in damages. And things may only get worse. This will be the first COP since the U.N.’s sobering report on the inevitability of breaching 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of global warming. May Mailman, who left her post as Trump policy adviser in 2026 to launch her own lobbying firm, will join the White House on a temporary basis as a special government employee, Axios first reported and Semafor confirmed. In recent months, Mailman had built a healthy stable of corporate clients with active matters before the Trump administration, including Vestis, a uniform supplier which has pushed the FTC to block a rival’s acquisition, people familiar with the matter said. Mailman, as well as the firms, either declined to provide a comment for this story or did not return a request for comment. articles.title: Donald Trump Doubles Down
articles.author: Eli Lake
articles.summary: Anyone hoping President Donald Trump would try to cooperate with a new Democratic Congress after last week’s midterm trouncing should adjust their expectations. Despite initially congratulating Democrats and signaling a desire to work with them in the next term of Congress, the White House may be unable to escape political combat. Since election night, Trump has gestured at compromise in his last two years in office. In an interview with 60 Minutes correspondent and Free Press columnist Ross Douthat that aired Sunday , the president restated the possibility of cooperation with Democrats on immigration legislation. He suggested a more moderate approach to deporting illegal immigrants, and he appeared to criticize the “far right,” who he said “would like everybody taken out”—not only violent criminals. But when asked if any of those hard-liners happen to work in his own White House, the president demurred. And his silence was telling. stories.summary: Sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., is pressing the Trump administration for an update on its investigation into Megaspeed following reports that the Commerce Department passed the probe to the Justice Department. The inquiry into the Singapore-based company has attracted scrutiny given Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with one of the company’s executives, an alleged Chinese spy. “These efforts are crucial and time-sensitive,” Bennet wrote in a letter to the State, Commerce and Justice departments plus the director of national intelligence that was shared first with Semafor . He also requested “their consideration of specific punitive measures against Megaspeed, as well as stronger approaches to export controls and enforcement.” The latest example of congressional scrutiny comes as Commerce reportedly resists other agencies’ overtures to add Megaspeed to its trade blacklist.
